From √alah (ascend); the offering 'that-which-ascends' (the smoke rising to YH). 287 occurrences — major sacrificial-term. KJV 'burnt-offering' captures the fire-aspect but loses the alah-link; ESV 'burnt-offering' retains the tradition. Concordant 'ascending-offering' (hyphenated) preserves the Hebrew-kernel where the offering's defining-feature is its smoke ascending wholly to YH (Lev 1; nothing of the animal returns to the offerer, distinguishing it from peace-offerings and sin-offerings).

Used (Gen 24:43; Ex 2:8; Pss 68:26 [25]; Pro 30:19; Song 1:3; 6:8; Isa 7:14). 7 occurrences. Hyphenated. The famous Isa 7:14 'Behold, the almah shall conceive' is the most-disputed occurrence; the LXX-translation 'parthenos' (virgin) became famous via Mat 1:23. The Hebrew kernel is 'young-marriageable-female', not specifically 'virgin'. Concordant 'young-maiden' preserves the marriageable-aspect; H1330 betulah is the technical-virgin and H5291 naarah is the broader 'young-woman'.
